_note: Draft English of Saadia's JA Tafsir on Bereshit 40 (cupbearer and baker dreams). Saadia-specific: v.1 'אד'נבא' = 'sinned/committed offense'; v.2 'רייס אלסקאה / רייס אלכבאזין' = 'chief of the cupbearers / chief of the bakers' (Saadia's gloss for שר המשקים / שר האפים); v.5 'חסב תפסירה' = 'according to its interpretation' (each dream interpretable on its own); v.8 'אן אלתפאסיר ללה' = 'interpretations belong to God' (Joseph's signature reply).

translations.1: And it was after these things, that the cupbearer of the king of Egypt and the baker offended their lord, the king of Egypt.
translations.2: And Pharaoh was wroth with his two servants — the chief of the cupbearers, and the chief of the bakers.
translations.3: And he placed them in custody, in the house of the chief of the executioners, in the prison — the place where Joseph was held.
translations.4: And the chief of the executioners appointed Joseph over them, to serve them; and they spent a time in the prison.
translations.5: Until the two of them saw a dream — each one his own, on one night; and the dream of each was according to its [own] interpretation — the cupbearer and the baker of the king of Egypt, the prisoners in the prison.
translations.6: And Joseph came in to them in the morning, and saw their faces — and behold, they were downcast.
translations.7: And he asked Pharaoh's servants who were with him in the custody of his master's house, saying: 'Why are your faces changed today?'
translations.8: They said to him: 'We have seen a dream — and there is no interpreter of it.' He said to them: 'Surely interpretations belong to God; but recount them to me.'
translations.9: And the chief of the cupbearers recounted his dream to Joseph, and said: 'I saw — and behold, a vine was before me.
translations.10: And on the vine were three branches; and as it budded, its blossoms came up, and its clusters ripened and became grapes.
translations.11: And Pharaoh's cup was in my hand; and I took the grapes, and squeezed them into it, and handed it to him.'
translations.12: Joseph said to him: 'This is its interpretation: the three branches are three days.
translations.13: Within three days, Pharaoh shall remember you, and shall restore you to your office; and you shall hand him his cup, as in your former manner, when you were his cupbearer.
translations.14: Only — remember me with you when your matter has been set right for you; and do me a kindness, and recall me to Pharaoh, and bring me out of this house.
translations.15: For I was stolen from the land of the Hebrews; and here too I have done nothing for which I should be put in confinement.'
translations.16: And when the chief of the bakers saw that he had interpreted it for good, he said to him: 'I too saw — and behold, three baskets of fine bread were upon my head;
translations.17: and in the topmost basket, of all the food of Pharaoh that the baker makes; and the bird was eating from them — from the baskets upon my head.'
translations.18: And Joseph answered, and said: 'This is its interpretation: the three baskets are three days.
translations.19: Within three days, Pharaoh shall lift up your head from your body, and impale you on a stake; and the bird shall eat of your flesh.'
translations.20: And it was on the third day — which was like Pharaoh's birthday — he made a feast for all his officers; and he remembered the chief of the cupbearers and the chief of the bakers among them.
translations.21: And he commanded that the chief of the cupbearers be restored to his cup-bearing; and he handed him his cup.
translations.22: And he impaled the chief of the bakers — as Joseph had interpreted for them.
translations.23: But the chief of the cupbearers did not remember Joseph; he forgot him.
